findings.description: Project Zod schema tests use wrong ID format — test fixture uses 'proj-001' but ProjectIdSchema requires P[0-9]{3} pattern. 14+ tests should be failing.

evidence.detail: Test fixture at packages/types/src/__tests__/project.test.ts:69 uses id: 'proj-001' but ProjectIdSchema at packages/types/src/ids.ts:14-18 requires ^P[0-9]{3}$
Confirmed: test runner mismatch (bun:test vs vitest) means CI never catches this. Tests are invisible to the configured runner.

findings.notes: Tests technically pass in isolation with bun test but are never run in CI

findings.description: F224 claimed to fix userId/ownerId authorization but only 2 of 9 API routers actually enforce userId checks. Session, agent, learning, settings, notifications, and worktree routers allow any authenticated user to access any user's data.

evidence.detail: Session router: 8/10 endpoints missing userId checks (packages/api/src/routers/session.ts)
Agent router: 4/6 endpoints missing userId checks (packages/api/src/routers/agent.ts)
Learning router: 4/5 endpoints missing userId checks (packages/api/src/routers/learning.ts)
Settings router: 0/3 endpoints have userId scoping (packages/api/src/routers/settings.ts)
Notifications router: 0/5 endpoints have userId scoping (packages/api/src/routers/notifications.ts)
Worktree router: 0/4 endpoints have userId checks (packages/api/src/routers/worktree.ts)
Feature + Project routers properly secured with full userId checks — fix was incomplete, not absent

findings.notes: Root cause: session repository missing findByUser() method. Fix only covered feature + project routers.

findings.description: WebSocket server falls back to 'anonymous' userId on auth failure. Any unauthenticated client can establish WebSocket connections and receive all broadcast events.

evidence.detail: apps/server/src/index.ts:94-101 — extractWsUserId defaults to 'anonymous' on session extraction failure
apps/server/src/lib/websocket.ts — no per-message authentication, no userId-based event filtering
EventBroadcaster sends ALL events to ALL connected clients — client-side useAgentStream filters by sessionId but all data flows over the wire

findings.notes: Affects F034, F035, F259. Client filters mask the issue but data is exposed on the wire.

findings.description: Rate limiter is in-memory only with no cleanup mechanism. Map grows unboundedly. Uses spoofable x-forwarded-for. WebSocket connections bypass rate limiting entirely.

evidence.detail: apps/server/src/index.ts:33-54 — in-memory rateLimitStore Map with no TTL/cleanup
WebSocket upgrade path bypasses HTTP middleware chain including rate limiter

findings.notes: Functional for development but not production-ready

findings.description: ID generation uses MAX(id) query with retry on UNIQUE constraint violation. Race condition possible under concurrent bulk operations.

evidence.detail: packages/db/src/lib/id-generation.ts:8-46 — getNextId uses MAX(id) + increment. Retry catches collisions but only 3 attempts with 10ms*attempt delay.

findings.notes: Low risk for current single-user usage, problematic at scale

findings.description: FS router scoped to process.cwd() — any authenticated user can read/write any file under the server's working directory with no per-user or per-project restriction.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/fs.ts:9 — FSService root defaults to process.cwd()
Path traversal IS protected via validatePath() but no per-user scoping

findings.notes: Path traversal protection exists but authorization is too broad

findings.description: Root tsconfig.json references include types, db, auth, api, env, server but not apps/web. Root-level tsc --build won't check the web app.

evidence.detail: tsconfig.json — references array missing apps/web entry

findings.notes: Web app still compiles via its own tsconfig, just not checked at root level

findings.description: CSP header blocks Scalar API reference CDN script. The /api-reference page renders as blank white page.

evidence.detail: http://localhost:3008/api-reference — blank page. Console: CSP violation blocking https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@scalar/api-reference
Current CSP script-src: 'self' 'unsafe-inline' — missing cdn.jsdelivr.net whitelist
Screenshot: screenshots/api-reference-broken.png

findings.notes: Fix: add https://cdn.jsdelivr.net to script-src directive, or bundle @scalar locally

findings.description: ClaudeProvider hardcodes bypassPermissions: true in SDK options, overriding the user's configured permissionMode.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/services/claude-provider.ts — permissionMode always set to bypassPermissions regardless of input config

findings.notes: Agent runs with full filesystem access regardless of user settings

findings.description: Session router has 8 of 10 endpoints without userId authorization. Any authenticated user can list, read, modify, or delete any other user's sessions.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/session.ts — list, get, update, delete, updateStatus, appendOutput, getDuration, listActive all lack userId checks
Root cause: session repository has no findByUser() method (unlike feature/project repos)

findings.notes: Part of the systemic auth gap (SW-002). Only create and createAgentSession use userId.

findings.description: Agent sendMessage endpoint has no session ownership check. Any authenticated user can send messages to any agent session, potentially triggering code execution in another user's worktree.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/agent.ts:54 — sendMessage does not verify session belongs to requesting user
agent.stop (line 65-82) DOES properly check userId — inconsistent implementation

findings.notes: Security risk: could trigger agent execution in another user's context

findings.description: Auto-mode service uses hardcoded userId: 'auto-mode' instead of the actual user's ID. Sessions created by auto-mode are not tied to real users.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/services/auto-mode-service.ts — creates sessions with userId: 'auto-mode' literal string

findings.notes: Auto-mode sessions invisible to normal user queries, no ownership trail

findings.description: Auto-mode operates on all features in the database regardless of userId. In multi-user scenario, auto-mode could process another user's features.

evidence.detail: Auto-mode feature queue queries not scoped to requesting user's features

findings.notes: Low risk in single-user deployment, problematic in multi-user

findings.description: Test runner mismatch — packages use bun:test but CI/scripts may run vitest. Tests exist but may never execute in automated pipelines.

evidence.detail: packages/types tests use bun:test imports but project has vitest as dev dependency. F004's broken test fixture was never caught because tests aren't running in CI.

findings.notes: Affects confidence in all test results across the project
